reading.title: Two Words, Two Messages
reading.purpose: See how a word choice can show whether you admire a person or not.
paras: Two words can describe the same action and still send different messages. Think about a neighbor who spends very little. If you call this person frugal, you are giving praise, because a frugal person plans carefully so that nothing is wasted. If you call the same person stingy, you are complaining, because a stingy person will not share even when there is plenty.

Many traits come in pairs like this one. An inquisitive student asks questions to learn something new. A nosy student asks about matters that belong to other people. A teammate who is assertive tells the group what she needs in a firm and polite way, but a bossy teammate simply gives orders and never listens.

The pairs also show up when people try new things. A daring hiker might take a hard trail after checking the weather and packing extra water. A foolhardy hiker would rush up the same trail in a storm, ignoring every warning sign. Most people admire the first hiker and worry about the second.

Calm behavior can be described in different ways too. An easygoing person stays relaxed when plans change, which makes group work smooth. A person who does nothing while everyone else works is called idle, and that is rarely a compliment.
When you write, ask yourself which message you mean. Choose the word that matches your opinion, and your readers will understand how you feel before they finish the sentence.

qs.q: In paragraph 1, a person who is "frugal" is someone who
choices: refuses to share even when there is plenty
spends money quickly on new things
plans carefully so that nothing is wasted
asks too many questions about other people
qs.why: The text says a frugal person "plans carefully so that nothing is wasted," and calls the word praise.

qs.q: Which sentence shows the difference between an assertive teammate and a bossy one?
choices: An inquisitive student asks questions to learn something new.
A teammate who is assertive tells the group what she needs in a firm and polite way, but a bossy teammate simply gives orders and never listens.
An easygoing person stays relaxed when plans change, which makes group work smooth.
Most people admire the first hiker and worry about the second.
qs.why: Only this sentence puts the two teammates side by side: one speaks up politely, the other gives orders and does not listen.

ev.text: A teammate who is assertive tells the group what she needs in a firm and polite way, but a bossy teammate simply gives orders and never listens.

qs.q: What does paragraph 3 suggest about the daring hiker?
choices: The hiker avoids every hard trail to stay safe.
The hiker climbs in a storm because danger is exciting.
The hiker is frightened and turns back early.
The hiker thinks about safety before taking a risk.
qs.why: The daring hiker checks the weather and packs extra water first, so the risk is planned, not careless.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: The words we choose can show whether we approve or disapprove of someone.
Every trait becomes a problem when a person has too much of it.
Writers should never describe people with strong words.
Words such as frugal and stingy mean exactly the same thing to every reader.
qs.why: Each paragraph pairs a kind word with a harsher one, and the last paragraph tells writers to pick the word that matches their opinion.
